original_question: For every integer k congruent to 1 modulo 4, prove or refute that the most avoided pattern of length k is the layered pattern with symmetric layer sizes (1, 2, ..., 2, 3, 2, ..., 2, 1).
target_in_paper: Section 4, “Are layered patterns the most easily avoided?”, specifically Steingrímsson’s report of Burstein’s Conjecture 9.11: for k ≡ 1 (mod 4), the most avoided pattern of length k is conjectured to have symmetric layer sizes (1,2,...,2,3,2,...,2,1). The surrounding setup on the preceding page makes clear that this is meant in the eventual/asymptotic sense of being avoided by most permutations of sufficiently large length n. ([vdoc.pub](https://vdoc.pub/documents/surveys-in-combinatorics-2013-7rqqau6gfgb0))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the right congruence class, k ≡ 1 (mod 4), and the right candidate layered shape, namely the symmetric layered pattern with a central layer of size 3 and all other nontrivial layers of size 2. So it is targeting Burstein’s Conjecture 9.11 as discussed in Section 4, not the neighboring k ≡ 3 (mod 4) discussion of Conjecture 9.12. ([vdoc.pub](https://vdoc.pub/documents/surveys-in-combinatorics-2013-7rqqau6gfgb0))
missing_details: The paper’s discussion is about classical permutation patterns; that scope should be stated explicitly in a stand-alone question. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1210.7320))

The phrase “most avoided” must be defined via avoidance numbers, e.g. Av_τ(n) = the number of permutations of length n that avoid the classical pattern τ. Without this, the claim is not mathematically self-contained. ([vdoc.pub](https://vdoc.pub/documents/surveys-in-combinatorics-2013-7rqqau6gfgb0))
The relevant comparison is among all classical patterns of length k, not merely among layered patterns of length k. ([vdoc.pub](https://vdoc.pub/documents/surveys-in-combinatorics-2013-7rqqau6gfgb0))

The asymptotic quantifier is missing: the surrounding context frames the question as which length-k pattern is avoided by most permutations of sufficiently large length n. A stand-alone formulation should therefore say explicitly that for every competing pattern σ of length k there exists N = N(σ,k) such that Av_σ(n) ≤ Av_λk(n) for all n ≥ N. ([vdoc.pub](https://vdoc.pub/documents/surveys-in-combinatorics-2013-7rqqau6gfgb0))

The layered pattern itself should be specified unambiguously: it is the direct sum of decreasing blocks with sizes (1,2,...,2,3,2,...,2,1), equivalently with (k-5)/4 layers of size 2 on each side of the central layer of size 3. ([vdoc.pub](https://vdoc.pub/documents/surveys-in-combinatorics-2013-7rqqau6gfgb0))

It is important to say that the claim is eventual rather than pointwise in n, because the paper immediately warns that finite-n rankings of avoidance counts can switch. ([vdoc.pub](https://vdoc.pub/documents/surveys-in-combinatorics-2013-7rqqau6gfgb0))
refined_question: Prove or refute the following conjecture. For each integer k ≡ 1 (mod 4), let λ_k be the classical layered permutation of length k obtained as the direct sum of decreasing blocks with sizes (1,2,...,2,3,2,...,2,1), so that there are (k-5)/4 blocks of size 2 on each side of the central block of size 3. If Av_τ(n) denotes the number of permutations of length n that avoid the classical pattern τ, is it true that for every classical pattern σ of length k there exists an integer N = N(σ,k) such that Av_σ(n) ≤ Av_λk(n) for all n ≥ N? Equivalently: for k ≡ 1 (mod 4), is λ_k eventually the most avoided classical pattern of length k? ([vdoc.pub](https://vdoc.pub/documents/surveys-in-combinatorics-2013-7rqqau6gfgb0))
justification: This rewrite stays as close as possible to the paper’s actual intent. Steingrímsson explicitly states in Section 4 that Burstein’s Conjecture 9.11 says that for k ≡ 1 (mod 4) the most avoided length-k pattern has symmetric layers (1,2,...,2,3,2,...,2,1). The immediately preceding setup on the same section frames the broader question as asking which pattern of length k is avoided by most permutations of sufficiently large length n, so the refined version makes that eventual quantifier explicit through the avoidance-count notation Av_τ(n). I also made “classical pattern” explicit because the paper says that, unless otherwise noted, the remainder is about classical patterns. Finally, I did not replace the conjecture by the weaker Stanley–Wilf-limit formulation, because the paper presents that only as a neighboring weaker conjecture, not as an equivalent reformulation of Burstein’s specific claim. ([vdoc.pub](https://vdoc.pub/documents/surveys-in-combinatorics-2013-7rqqau6gfgb0))
